answer: Remote hardware attestation curbs a Sybil spiral by requiring each agent to bind its key inside a Trusted Execution Environment and submit a chip-unique quote over an epoch nonce. This carves a cost canyon where attackers incur the scarce expense of dedicated physical silicon per identity instead of spawning virtual clones. A limitation is that side-channel exploits can leak platform signing keys like flaws inside an opal, letting one compromised chip forge countless fake agents.
